ruling: - **R45. How cloud sessions delete branches.** Owner 14:25 CST Nov 11: "im good with either an actions workflow or a github token -- github token seems better? im very ambivalent to tokens being in all my cloud sessions its just a github token". Measured 14:21 CST: the cloud relay drops a branch-delete push; a new-branch push works. Origin holds 2,338 branches (331 under archive/), because a cloud archive push adds a branch and the delete fails. Probe github-projects-probe, 14:23 CST: the cloud cannot read or write GitHub Projects. 1. The owner makes one GitHub token (repo and project scopes) and adds it to the cloud environment as SHIV_GITHUB_TOKEN. 2. A session tests one branch delete and one Projects read with it. The relay, not GitHub, refuses today, so the test may fail. 3. If the relay passes it, deletes go through one home that applies the Oct 30 grant (last commit on main or an archive branch), and the guard reads that route. If it refuses, the same token becomes a GitHub repository secret, and an Actions workflow does the deletes and the table on GitHub's side. Result, 15:04 CST: the relay refuses writes made with the owner's token too (REST ref delete 403, "Write access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy"; GraphQL 403). REST reads pass. So the fallback holds: an Actions workflow deletes with GitHub's own token, and the Projects table needs the owner's token as a repository secret. Ruled g, owner 15:19 CST Nov 11: "i think my answer is G right -- the table view isn't too releveant if we have other ways around it right?". 1. GitHub's auto-delete setting removes a merged PR's branch. 2. An Actions workflow with GitHub's own token deletes the rest the Oct 30 grant allows. 3. A check derives each roadmap step's status from live PRs on the roadmap branch; no Projects table. The owner's token is not needed. The docs say the relay blocks deletes, tags and GraphQL for every token; only a self-hosted environment skips the relay. Scope ruled k, owner 15:31 CST Nov 11: "sure k is fine". One shared branch-sweep action in claude-settings, called from each repo's existing CI at each push to main, with that repo's own token; the R44 child-repo sweep adds the call. Auto-delete of merged PR branches is on in all 8 shivinate7 repos and all 7 ssemwal-cdc repos (owner's gh runs, 15:26 and 15:31 CST). Rulesets, ruled r, owner 16:43 CST Nov 11: "r". In the R44 child-repo sweep, a session on the owner's computer moves every repo's main to a ruleset that requires only all-jobs-passed and blocks deletion and force-push of main. Cause: a classic rule with many checks failed to save (owner, 16:39 CST). Owner 16:49 CST, in the coordinator's chat (coordinator-relayed): "yes with bypass": the ruleset may also let the repository admin role skip the checks on pull requests only. The grant names rulesets, so it lands in the repo's standing grants beside the Oct 30 grant (draft PR #2606). The merge tool reads rulesets, ruled c, owner 19:49 CST Nov 11: "c is prob best". Today merge/merge.py protection_names reads main's old branch protection and stops every merge when it is gone. Step merge-reads-ruleset makes it read main's ruleset first and the old protection second; skills/project-ops/scripts/protect.py, which sets classic protection today, will set the ruleset. It lands before the sweep removes any old protection. Once every repo has a ruleset, the old-protection read is deleted. Option c carried the label "Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo"; he chose it over that ruling. No GitHub Issues, ruled p', owner 16:44 CST Nov 11: "agreed on p", then "yea" when asked whether he meant the refuter's revised p'. g is mostly built: skills/roadmap/build.py derives live and done from PRs (decision stalled-steps). 1. Nobody types doing; triage's build sets status from live PRs. 2. Triage closes the stale drafts on build.py's list once, then at each batch. 3. A guard refuses a lane PR whose branch or title names no step id (45 of the newest 100 open PRs named one by branch). Home: decision for the delete route (new); D1 for the table.
